title: Build each merchant's purchases from its boarding data

blocks.text: Your gateway builds purchases for many merchants. Each merchant arrives with the properties file the acquirer's boarding team filled in: terminal, merchant ID, category code, currency, name, city, country, and one `acquirer.<network>` line per card network the merchant may accept. Since the gateway started taking Mastercard and Discover cards, the acquirer has reported two kinds of bad purchases: some reach it with no acquiring institution ID, or with the wrong network's, and some show merchants in cities that don't exist.
`Boarding.purchase` in `src/main/java/com/example/practice/Boarding.java` already builds the request. Finish the two methods marked `TODO`:

items: `acquirerId(network)`: the merchant's ID for that network. When the merchant has none, the purchase must not be built: throw `IllegalArgumentException`.
`nameAndLocation()`: field 43 for any merchant the boarding team may send you, short or long.

blocks.text: The tests pack each purchase with the course packager and read field 43 back as a host does. About ten lines in total.

cases.says: a Visa purchase carries the merchant's Visa acquirer ID, terminal, merchant ID and amount, and the host reads its name, city and country back
each network's purchase carries the acquirer ID boarded for that network, whatever case the network name is written in
a purchase on a network the merchant has no acquirer ID for is refused instead of being built without field 32
a network nobody boarded is refused rather than given another network's acquirer ID
a short merchant name is padded so the city and country stay in their positions
a merchant name longer than its positions is cut, so field 43 still packs and the city stays in place
a city longer than its positions is cut as well, so the country stays at the end of the field

concepts: Field 43 is read by position, so each part is cut and padded to the width the specification gives it.
Per-network values such as the acquirer ID come from configuration, and a missing one must stop the request, because ISOMsg.set with null silently removes the field.
The fields ISO 8583 defines read the same on every network, so one builder makes them with the network as a parameter; per-network copies drift.
